source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item says PSU Inventory, the Master Procedure requests Manager LogService Entries through malformed placeholders, and DeepSeek instead requests Chassis Power. These are three different resources with different fields, privacy risks and acceptance criteria.

blocked_analysis.analysis: No source authority identifies which of the three resource scopes is intended. Selecting one would invent testcase identity, so owner correction is required before even a read-only request can be safely classified for execution.

review_improvement: Makes the three-way identity conflict explicit and prohibits plausible but unauthorized endpoint substitution until one domain-specific contract is approved.
independent_technical_reasoning: Resource identity determines what success means: a LogEntry collection proves event access, a Power resource exposes live electrical/PSU structures, and inventory requires stable component identity such as model/part/serial. The same readable/command-success criterion cannot reconcile them. The multiline placeholder defect further prevents executing the procedure literally, but repairing it would still query the wrong domain for the title. Therefore even GET is unsafe from an audit-integrity perspective until the owner chooses one scope.
